title: Government's Response to SPH Media Trust's Inflated Circulation Numbers
what_it_is: Government's Response to SPH Media Trust's Inflated Circulation Numbers

sections.label: Questions on SPH Media circulation data
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister about the status of investigations, corrective actions, audit scope, and effects on funding for SPH Media Trust's circulation data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information with regard to the alleged inconsistencies in circulation data at SPH Media Trust (SMT) (a) what is the status of the internal investigation and when will the detailed findings be made public; (b) what are the immediate corrective actions taken; and (c) how will this affect the Government’s long-term commitment to SMT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information with regard to the overstated reporting of newspaper circulation data by SPH Media Trust (SMT) (a) what is the breakdown of discrepancy in circulation numbers for each of SMT’s publication titles; (b) what is the extent to which the vernacular language publications are affected; (c) whether there will be a fuller audit to cover the period of review prior to September 2020; and (d) how will the results of the audit and other investigations affect the Ministry’s committed funding of SMT in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information whether the Ministry has reviewed (i) the duration which SPH Media Trust conducted the practice of over-printing, double counting of circulation numbers and then destroying these copies (ii) the impact of such practice on digital circulation (iii) the effect of this practice on its financial statements and if it was deemed material, including when it was a listed company and (iv) the undertaking of regulatory actions against current or former employees and board directors for any breaches.

sections.label: Accountability and funding review questions
sections.summary: Questions ask what actions will hold SPH Media Trust accountable and whether the $900 million funding announcement will be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) what actions will be taken against SPH Media Trust (SMT) to hold it accountable for the inconsistencies in the reported daily circulation data; and (b) whether there will be a review to the Government’s previous announcement that it will fund SMT and provide up to $900 million in funding support over the next five years.

sections.label: Funding formula and police referral questions
sections.summary: Questions ask how the Ministry will review its funding formula and whether individuals behind inflated circulation figures were referred to Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) how will the Ministry review its formula to fund SPH Media Trust in light of the inconsistencies in circulation data; (b) to what extent will this review be shared publicly including the names of individuals who are found to have engaged in deceptive behaviours and the relevant follow-up actions taken.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) whether individuals involved in initiating and perpetuating the inflated circulation figures in SPH Media Trust have been referred to the Police for further investigation; and (b) if so, how many have been referred to the Police for further investigation.

sections.label: SMT overstated circulation numbers
sections.summary: SMT's review found circulation numbers in some months were overstated by up to 90,000 average daily copies.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In its review, SMT found that circulation numbers in some months during the period under review were overstated by up to 90,000 average daily copies.

sections.label: No funds disbursed to SMT
sections.summary: No funds have been disbursed, the Government had no funding relationship with SMT before FY2022, so the findings have no bearing on public funds.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Up to now, we have not disbursed any funds.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Moreover, the Government did not have a funding relationship with SMT before FY2022.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Therefore, the findings of SMT’s internal review of circulation data from September 2020 to March 2022 have no bearing on public funds.

sections.label: MCI review start date
sections.summary: MCI's review started after SMT shared its internal report with the Government on 9 January 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: MCI’s review started after SMT shared its internal report with the Government on 9 January 2023.

sections.label: SMT digital content and trust
sections.summary: An MCI survey found over 70% accessed SMT digital content in 2021, and 77% trusted The Straits Times.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Based on an MCI survey, more than 70% of respondents accessed SMT’s digital content at least a few times a week in 2021, a jump of almost 30% since 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Reuters Institute Digital News Report indicated that 77% of respondents expressed trust in The Straits Times in 2021, up from 70% in 2018.

sections.label: Vernacular media and tech funding
sections.summary: Funds would preserve vernacular media and, in initial years, about 40% would go to tech and digital talent.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The funds would be used also for the preservation of vernacular media – sustaining the vernacular newsrooms and developing new content formats like videos and podcasts to reach younger audiences.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I had also informed Parliament that in its initial years, we expect SMT to spend approximately 40% of the funding on tech investments and digital talent.

sections.label: No change to SMT funding
sections.summary: No public monies were lost and there is no change to the decision or amount of SMT funding.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Specifically, no public monies have been lost; there is no change to the decision to provide funding support to SMT; and there is no change to the amount of funding for SMT.

sections.label: SMT review and funding release
sections.summary: MCI expects SMT's audit findings, no funding released yet, and funding follows KPIs and safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Government welcomes the Board’s resolve to examine the findings of its internal review and to put SMT on the right footing.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: MCI expects SMT to share the findings of its Audit and Risk Committee’s investigation with us.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: SMT’s Board and management must also be mindful of their public duties, their responsibility to maintain the public’s trust in their newsrooms and journalists, and the need to discharge these responsibilities in a diligent and timely manner.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I understand that no funding has been released to SMT yet, but when will the first tranche for FY2022 be released in light of the current situation?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And once we are satisfied that the KPIs have been properly set as well as the safeguards that I had explained earlier have been properly included in the agreement, we will release the funding.

sections.label: SMT police referral and safeguards
sections.summary: SMT must refer any evidence of broken laws to Police, and the funding commitment does not change.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If there is any evidence of laws having been broken, it will be the obligation of SMT to refer the matter to the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There are safeguards in place and we will exercise them as necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But as it stands right now, our commitment to fund the capability development of SMT does not change.

sections.label: Circulation overstatement not right
sections.summary: Circulation numbers were not key to funding, but overstating them is not right.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The circulation numbers may not have been our key consideration in providing funding, but the overstatement of these numbers is not right.

sections.label: Board sharing audit findings
sections.summary: The board must share the Audit and Risk Committee's findings with MCI after completing its investigation and rectify what needs rectifying.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The board will have to share the Audit and Risk Committee's findings with MCI after it has completed its investigation and rectify what needs to be rectified.

sections.label: SMT funding review conclusion
sections.summary: The review concluded that the reasons for funding SMT remain valid and the funding level set aside will not change.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The conclusion of that review is that the reasons for funding SMT remain valid and the level of funding that we have set aside will not change.

sections.label: Compensation for lower value takeover
sections.summary: Taking over something worth less cannot be expected to be provided more compensation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If something is worth less and I have to take over something that is worth less, surely I cannot be expected to be provided more compensation.

sections.label: Questioning SMT funding amount
sections.summary: We must ask ourselves whether the amount decided to fund SMT's capability development is the right amount.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: At the end of the day, we have to ask ourselves: is the amount that we have decided to fund SMT's capability development the right amount?
